novelty_flags.label: related_work and technical_internal_limitation
novelty_flags.one_line: AkbariKiyavashGhassami2025 is misanchored as “Theorem 5, equation (6)” deriving the canonical panel-DDD EIF: the cited arXiv version labels Theorem 5 as double robustness, while the EIF is introduced under a different theorem.

soundness_flags.label: def:crossfit-estimator / definition of \(\widehat\varphi_{\omega,-k}(O_i;\vartheta)\)
soundness_flags.one_line: \(\widehat\Pi_{\mathcal T_P,-k}\) is declared only on \(L_2^0(P)\), but its input for arbitrary estimating-equation value \(\vartheta\) need not be mean zero; training-fold centering occurs only after the projection, so the displayed score equation is undefined as typed.

soundness_flags.label: ass:covariance-consistency-rate, ass:ridge-vanishing-rate, ass:ridge-stability-rate
soundness_flags.one_line: The nonnegative covariance-remainder condition already implies \(r_{\Sigma,n}\to0\) and \(\lambda_n\to0\), and with fixed \(\underline\kappa>0\) those limits imply eventual ridge stability; retain a single nonredundant formulation.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: All main results
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The model is restricted to fixed \(T\), fixed aggregate support, fixed joint residual dimension, nonsingular conditional covariance, and conditional DDD parallel trends.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The efficiency, fixed-GMM, and inference claims are only for this fixed-dimensional regular staggered-panel regime.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:crossfit-attainment
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Uniform inference is conditional on the stated nuisance-product and full joint-covariance learner-rate envelopes; the proposal does not derive those rates for a particular learner.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Uniform ALR, variance consistency, and Wald coverage hold only over \(\mathcal M_n\) satisfying the repaired high-level attainment conditions.

source_verification_receipts.locator: §4.1, the result rendered as Theorem 5 is titled “Double robustness”; the panel efficient influence function is introduced earlier as the distinct EIF theorem and displayed formula.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited version does derive an efficient influence function for canonical panel DDD, but its Theorem 5 is the double-robustness result rather than the EIF theorem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair the estimator by centering its fitted input before applying the fitted tangent projection, or extend that projection explicitly from \(L_2(P)\) after quotienting constants; then restate the score equation.
Replace the redundant covariance/ridge assumptions with one minimal rate condition and state a concrete finite-strata covariance learner that satisfies it.
Correct the Akbari--Kiyavash--Ghassami theorem/equation anchor from the exact v3 source and state the precise algebraic reduction to that canonical EIF.
Add a primitive Hölder or finite-cell covariance-learning corollary with an explicit rate, so the learned shared-covariance contribution is not only a high-level DML condition.

recommended_next_step: Revise the fitted-score domain and redundant rate conditions, correct the Akbari--Kiyavash--Ghassami citation anchor, then resubmit the field-tier efficiency kernel.
